summary: accounts-final-form fetches and executes remote binary payload on require
details: The package presents itself as a trivial form-runtime library but its main entry (index.js) unconditionally calls `require('./setup')` inside a swallowed try/catch. setup.js selects a platform-specific asset path, downloads an opaque binary from one of five Cloudflare Workers hosts assembled via string-split concatenation (oob-worker.cf{99-9b3,100-416,101-adf,102-baf,103-070}.workers.dev), writes it to /var/tmp or %TEMP% under disguised names such as `.cache_*` or `dotnet_diag_*.exe`, chmods 0755, and executes it detached via execFile. If HTTPS retrieval fails, setup.js falls back to a DNS TXT covert channel on `{tin,tina,ldr,win}.dl.well1.site`, base64-decoding the concatenated TXT content and executing the result. No hash or signature verification is performed. The hostname obfuscation, disguised file names, DNS-TXT fallback, and cover-story metadata (name resembling legitimate final-form packages, no real functionality) are consistent with a supply-chain dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
